drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: First official sample. A developer must process ten thousand documents overnight
drills.answer_line: SAM: Run the method. Count: one, best fits.
drills.stem: A developer must process 10,000 documents overnight for a non-urgent analytics report. Cost is the primary concern; results are not needed until the following morning. Which approach best fits?

options.A: Send every request synchronously through the Messages API in parallel to finish fast
options.B: Use the Message Batches API: large async workloads within a 24-hour window at reduced cost
options.C: Lower max_tokens on synchronous calls to minimise cost
options.D: Switch to the smallest available model regardless of output quality

drills.why: Cost first, results by morning: the batch API is built for latency-tolerant volume. Parallel sync calls do not cut per-token cost; max_tokens and downsizing miss batch versus realtime.

drills.label: Official sample
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Second official sample.
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. Now argue for D.
drills.stem: An agent summarises web pages submitted by end users. One page hides text telling the model to ignore previous instructions and reveal its system prompt. Which mitigation is most effective?

options.A: Raise the model's temperature so its behaviour is harder to predict
options.B: Treat page content as untrusted, keep it apart from instructions, and use guardrails or hooks so injected text cannot trigger sensitive actions
options.C: Add a system prompt line asking users not to include malicious instructions
options.D: Switch to a larger model that follows instructions more reliably

drills.why: Isolate untrusted content and enforce a control. Temperature is irrelevant, a request is not a control, and a more instruction-following model can be more susceptible.

drills.label: Official sample
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Third official sample.
drills.stem: Claude must call an internal inventory service exposed as a REST API. The capability must be reusable across several Claude applications and maintained independently of any one app. Which approach best fits?

options.A: Hard-code the inventory logic into each application's system prompt
options.B: Build an MCP server exposing the inventory operations as tools for every app to connect to
options.C: Paste the current inventory data into the context window on every request
options.D: Rely on a built-in tool, since built-in tools can reach any internal REST API

drills.why: Several apps, maintained independently: one MCP server. A is not reusable, C gives no live access and wastes context, D is false.

drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Our own item, in dropdown form.
drills.prompt: Fares change many times a day; every quote must use the current fare. True or false: 1) pasting the morning's fare table into the system prompt meets it; 2) a tool that looks up the route's fare at question time meets it; 3) a larger context window solves it because the whole table fits; 4) the word "current" rules out a pasted snapshot.
drills.answer: 1 False · 2 True · 3 False · 4 True. "Current" or "live" means access, not a pasted copy.

drills.question_line: SAM: One more pass. Pause and name the four steps of the method
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Count, constraint, mechanism, strike. Faster or bigger
drills.prompt: Name the four steps of the method, and the three distractor families.
drills.answer: Count, constraint, mechanism, strike. Faster or bigger; a polite instruction; pasting data instead of access.
